body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md step 5 and plugins/ok-conduct/hooks/session-start + hooks.json; ran the hook with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=plugins/ok-conduct (prints 'ok-conduct 1.20.0 (Tapir) is installed for this user'). The skill diverges: step 5 says 'Read it from the ok-conduct SessionStart hook's injected context line ... ok-conduct <version> is installed for this user', but that line is written once, when the hook fires (hooks.json matcher 'startup|clear|compact'), so it records what was installed at session start, not what is installed now. /ok step 1 runs 'claude plugin update <name>@ok-plugins' for the conduct mid-session and says changes take effect after /reload-plugins; after that update (and after /reload-plugins, which fires no SessionStart), /ok-version reports the old conduct as both governing (step 4, from the output style) and installed (step 5), so the drift between the new installed conduct and the old governing one is invisible. Step 2 by contrast reads the installed plugin live with 'claude plugin list --json'. The story promises: 'see which plugin version actually governs my current session or project, alongside what is installed, so that version drift is visible'. Fix direction: read the installed conduct stamp from disk at report time (the ok-conduct@ entry's installPath from 'claude plugin list --json' + output-styles/ok-conduct.md, line 'Conduct version:').

Reviewed step 2 of plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md: 'Run claude plugin list --json and find the entry whose id begins ok@. Report its version.' Ran 'claude plugin list --json' (read-only): it lists one entry per install, including project-scoped installs for other projects, each with scope and projectPath; e.g. 'rimsky@rimsky-docs 1.6.0 user' and 'rimsky@rimsky-docs 1.0.0 project /Users/patrick/Documents/projects/research/rimsky/crimefinder', and typescript-lsp@ appears seven times. When ok@ is installed at user scope and also at project scope for some project, the list holds several ok@ entries at different versions, and the skill names no rule to pick the one that applies to this session (user scope, or project scope whose projectPath is this project, enabled). A session following the text can report another project's install as 'installed'. The story promises: 'which plugin version actually governs my current session or project, alongside what is installed, so that version drift is visible'. Saw: no selection rule; the reported 'installed' value is whichever ok@ entry the agent hits first.

Reviewed where /ok-version ships and what points to it. The skill lives only in the carried family (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md); plugins/ok/skills holds only 'ok', and plugins/ok-conduct ships no skill. Converge materializes it into .claude/skills/ok-version/ (scratch-project diagnose before bootstrap listed 'DRIFT: missing: .claude/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md'), so it exists only in a project that integrates ok-planner. The conduct is personal and governs 'in every project and session the user runs' (concept conduct), and /ok step 3 accepts a declined bootstrap as 'not integrated (declined)'. Yet plugins/ok-conduct/hooks/session-start tells every session: '/ok-version reports the conduct actually governing.' In a project with no ok-planner estate, that verb does not exist, so a suite consumer there has no way to see which conduct version governs the session beside the installed one, and the hook points at a command the user cannot run. The story promises: 'see which plugin version actually governs my current session or project, alongside what is installed, so that version drift is visible'. Saw: no version surface outside an integrated project; the conduct hook names one that is absent.
